name: pwritev2
synopsis: ssize_t pwritev2(int fd, const struct iovec *iov, int iovcnt, off_t offset, int flags);
description: The pwritev2() system call writes data from multiple buffers to a file descriptor at a specified offset, combining the functionality of writev() and pwrite(2). It supports additional flags to modify behavior, such as atomicity or non-blocking operations, and ensures the file offset is not changed.

parameters.name: iov
parameters.description: Array of iovec structures describing the buffers to write from

parameters.name: iovcnt
parameters.description: Number of elements in the iov array

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: File offset at which to perform the write

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to modify the write behavior, such as RWF_NOWAIT

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes written
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: The sum of the iov_len values overflows an ssize_t value, or iovcnt is less than zero or greater than the permitted maximum
An unknown flag is specified in flags
Errors as per read(2), write(2), and lseek(2)

bugs: Linux 5.9 and Linux 5.10 have a bug where preadv2() with the RWF_NOWAIT flag may return 0 even when not at end of file; similar issues might affect pwritev2.
examples: char *str0 = "hello "; char *str1 = "world\n"; struct iovec iov[2]; iov[0].iov_base = str0; iov[0].iov_len = strlen(str0); iov[1].iov_base = str1; iov[1].iov_len = strlen(str1); ssize_t nwritten = pwritev2(fd, iov, 2, offset, flags);
